name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_SEQ_Q01 - Chronological sequence of steps in IVF-ET procedure

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following steps of the In Vitro Fertilisation followed by Embryo Transfer (IVF-ET) programme in the correct chronological sequence:

(1) Transfer of early embryo (up to 8 blastomeres) into the fallopian tube or embryo with more than 8 blastomeres into the uterus
(2) Collection of ova from the wife/donor and sperms from the husband/donor
(3) Further embryonic development inside the female reproductive tract
(4) Induced formation of zygote under simulated conditions in the laboratory

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In vitro fertilisation followed by embryo transfer (IVF-ET), popularly known as the test tube baby programme, involves fertilisation outside the body under conditions similar to those inside the body, followed by transfer of the resulting embryo into the female reproductive tract.

Step 2: Ordering the Stages Chronologically
The process begins with the collection of gametes—ova from the wife or donor and sperms from the husband or donor (2). Next, these gametes are induced to form a zygote under simulated conditions in the laboratory (4). Thereafter, the zygote or early embryo with up to 8 blastomeres is transferred into the fallopian tube (ZIFT), or an embryo with more than 8 blastomeres is transferred into the uterus (IUT) (1). Finally, the transferred embryo completes its further development inside the female reproductive tract (3).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct chronological sequence of steps in the IVF-ET programme is (2) → (4) → (1) → (3).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_SEQ_Q02 - Chronological order of reproductive health milestones in India

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following events related to reproductive health and population milestones in India in the correct chronological order from earliest to latest:

(1) Legalisation of Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) in India with strict conditions
(2) Initiation of national-level 'family planning' programmes in India
(3) Enactment of the Medical Termination of Pregnancy (Amendment) Act
(4) Crossing of the 1.2 billion population mark in India

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
India's reproductive health policies, legislative frameworks, and demographic milestones occurred over several decades, beginning with early family planning initiatives and progressing to updated abortion laws and population census records.

Step 2: Assigning Dates to Each Event
National-level 'family planning' programmes were initiated in India in 1951 (2). Subsequently, the Government of India legalised Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) in 1971 with strict conditions to prevent misuse (1). Later, India's population crossed the 1.2 billion mark in May 2011 (4). Finally, the Medical Termination of Pregnancy (Amendment) Act was enacted in 2017 to reduce illegal abortions and maternal mortality and morbidity (3).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Ordering these events from earliest (1951) to latest (2017) gives the chronological sequence (2) → (1) → (4) → (3).
